entries.title: Draft: bounded order parameter and pressure double limit
entries.statement: DRAFT, author-proved special case, independent review pending; no claim that P0309 is solved. For beta>0 and symmetric M_N with |M_N|<=N, pointwise convergence near zero of p_N(h)=log E exp(beta*h*M_N)/(beta*N) implies lim_{h down to 0}liminf_N p_N'(h)=lim_{h down to 0}limsup_N p_N'(h)=p'_+(0). Every finite-N response at h=0 is zero. Remaining scope: Independent review; full Riesz pressure cusp not proved.
assumptions: Fixed finite beta>0
Probability laws symmetric in M_N
Pointwise finite pressure limit for every h in an open interval about zero

entries.title: Draft: pressure slope and the exact Fourier-event rate threshold
entries.statement: DRAFT, author-proved special case, independent review pending; no claim that P0309 is solved. Fix beta>0 and h0>0. For each N let M_N have a symmetric law and |M_N|<=N. Assume p_N(h)=log E exp(beta*h*M_N)/(beta*N) converges to finite p(h) for every |h|<h0. Put A_N=M_N/N and m=p'_+(0). For every 0<=a<m, liminf_N log P(A_N>=a)/N=0. For every m<a<=1, limsup_N log P(A_N>=a)/N is strictly negative. Conversely, a zero lower exponential rate at any a>0 implies m>=a. No assertion is made at a=m. Remaining scope: Independent review; subexponential crystalline-event mass for actual Riesz gases remains unproved.
assumptions: Fixed finite beta>0; an open pressure interval about zero
The standalone statement's bounded order variable and exact law symmetry
Pointwise finite pressure convergence throughout that interval
Full-law expectations; no conditioned crystalline-branch substitution

entries.title: Draft: cell Fourier response requires local uniform integrability and Gibbs closure
entries.statement: DRAFT, author-proved special case, independent review pending; no claim that P0309 is solved. Let Gamma be a full rank lattice in R^d with bounded fundamental cell C and nonzero reciprocal vector G. Let Gamma-invariant canonical periodic laws mu_k be tiled by K_k cells with N_k=rho*K_k*|C| particles, fixed rho>0, and N_k->infinity. Suppose m_k=N_k^(-1) E_mu_k sum_x cos(G.x)->m>0. If their periodically lifted laws converge locally weakly to P, local counts n_C are uniformly integrable, and P has no points on boundary C, then E_P sum_{x in C}cos(G.x)=rho*|C|*m>0. P breaks full translation invariance. For laws from fields h_k->0, the unpinned Gibbs conclusion needs a separately established closure theorem for the specified kernels. Remaining scope: Independent review; Riesz tightness/UI and long-range Gibbs closure not established here; a single Fourier mode does not classify a full crystal.
assumptions: Compatible finite tori and Gamma-invariant laws
N=rho*K_N*|C|
G nonzero reciprocal vector of Gamma
Positive diagonal response limit
Local weak convergence
Uniform integrability of local counts
Zero limiting boundary count
Gibbs closure is an additional assumption only for the Gibbs conclusion

entries.title: Draft refuted route: an exponentially rare crystalline branch need not order after depinning
entries.statement: DRAFT, author-proved special case, independent review pending; no claim that P0309 is solved. Fix beta,c>0 and 0<a<=1. Let M_N/N have probabilities 1/(2+exp(c*N)), 1/(2+exp(c*N)), exp(c*N)/(2+exp(c*N)) at a,-a,0. Then p_N(h)=log E exp(beta*h*M_N)/(beta*N) tends to p(h)=max(a*|h|-c/beta,0), with p'_+(0)=0, although conditioning on the positive branch gives response a. This refutes an inference; it is not a Riesz counterexample. Remaining scope: Independent review. This refutes a conditional-branch inference only; it is not a Riesz counterexample.
assumptions: Specified finite probability laws
Fixed finite beta,c>0

entries.title: Draft: full-law circular Bragg intensity implies positive pressure slope
entries.statement: DRAFT, author-proved special case, independent review pending; no claim that P0309 is solved. Fix beta>0 and h0>0. For every N let S_N be complex, |S_N|<=N, and its law invariant under S_N->exp(i*theta)*S_N for every real theta. Assume p_N(h)=log E exp(beta*h*Re S_N)/(beta*N) converges to finite p(h) for every |h|<h0. If liminf_N E|S_N/N|^2>=b^2 with 0<b<=1, then p'_+(0)>=b. The expectation must be under the full zero-field law. No particle independence or Gaussian assumption is needed. Remaining scope: Independent review. The actual unrestricted Riesz full-law moment, pressure existence, local-limit control and Gibbs closure are not proved.
assumptions: Fixed finite beta>0; an open pressure interval about zero
The standalone statement's bounded order variable and exact law symmetry
Pointwise finite pressure convergence throughout that interval
Full-law expectations; no conditioned crystalline-branch substitution

entries.title: Refuted route: conditional crystalline order is insufficient for spontaneous order
entries.statement: Refuted inference, not a theorem: a positive order parameter in a Gibbs law conditioned on a selected crystalline branch does not by itself imply a positive vanishing-field response in the unrestricted zero-field law. The probability and entropy cost of that branch in the full partition function are missing hypotheses. The explicit three-state family in this bundle has branch response a>0 but full pressure slope zero.
assumptions: A branch-conditioned law is different from the unrestricted law

entries.title: P0309 remaining gap: full-law nonzero Fourier order at finite temperature
entries.statement: OPEN proof obligation, current openness UNKNOWN: for a specified unrestricted three-dimensional Coulomb or Riesz Gibbs model at fixed finite beta and density rho, prove that some nonzero crystalline Fourier-response event has zero exponential probability cost, or prove a positive full-law Bragg-intensity liminf. The pressure bridge then also needs pressure-limit existence, local uniform integrability and closure of the specified unpinned Gibbs equations. One nonzero mode only establishes translation breaking; BCC/FCC selection and a full rank periodic crystal require further results.
assumptions: Full unrestricted Riesz law, not a harmonic or defect-free restriction
Correct short-range or neutralized long-range specification must be fixed

relations.rationale: C2 uses the finite pressure limit and right slope defined in C1, then splits the bounded exponential moment.
C5 obtains a positive real Fourier-tail probability through circular averaging and applies C2's zero-rate-implies-slope statement.
C1 can select a positive-response diagonal; C3 separately supplies the local-limit obligations needed to retain it.
The three-state weights yield conditional branch response a but full pressure max(a|h|-c/beta,0), whose right slope is zero.
C5 supplies a bridge only after its full-law Bragg and pressure hypotheses are established for the actual Riesz model.
Each p_N is differentiable on an open interval and convex because its second derivative is beta*Var_h(M_N)/N; the tangent inequalities give C1's secant squeeze.

The exact prior attempt explicitly bounds only a Gaussian approximation conditional on a lattice, leaving defects, anharmonic fluctuations and alternative configurations; these do not provide C5's full-law expectation.
The scoped pressure and Fourier-response bridge addresses a necessary translation-breaking component of the intake; it does not prove BCC/FCC classification or the full phase diagram.
